norms.text: The furnace is built new each season and broken open for the bloom.
Each digger goes home to a different village at the end of the season.

taboos.text: Working the deep end of the seep.
Asking a digger which village sent them.

values.text: A full stack of cakes on the bank before the rains.
Iron for the road crews, paid in coin.

contempts.text: Visitors who come to watch the digging.

place.text: A seep in the ferns and a clay furnace; a place to work and leave.

work.text: Iron cakes lifted from the mud and smelted for road crews. Necessary work that shames whoever does it.

danger.text: Leeches in the seep; something in the deep end that the diggers will not name.

rumour.text: The seep is giving out: smaller cakes, further from the path, each season.

directions.text: Up the path to the road; west to the Mile House of the Eagle, then Cartwright's Cross.

addressTerms.text: Visitor, to anyone off the road; crew by name.

neverSaid.text: That the work brings any pride.

grievances.text: The seep is worked out and the season's pay is the same.

views.text: Road folk buy the iron and look away from those who dig it.

dissent.text: She works the bellows from first light and feels the shame of the work most; she says so (record notes).
